And then the camp was thrown into confusion.
And when he had burned the siege-engines, the materials of the siege-works, and the grain, al-Mu'tasim went down to Baghdad.
And the nobles came out to meet him and received him, though they were not pleased with him because of his harshness.
And when he was confirmed in the kingdom,
he began to build splendid buildings for his residence, and water basins and gardens for his recreation.
For he was very robust in his body,
and occupied with drinking wine.
And when he saw that the Zutt robbers, who were in the bays of the marshes into which the Euphrates and Tigris flow,
could not be overcome by the troops because they fought in light boats (qarquras),
he sent for the Egyptians whom he had captured from Egypt, who were accustomed to water.
For they used to dive like fish,
and suddenly strike the Zutt with javelins and rip them open.
And thus the Zutt were conquered,
and they and their families were captured,
and they perished in Baghdad in prison.
At this time there appeared in the Sea of Bahrain a huge fish,
its length was about one mile.
And for three months it troubled the sea,
and those who dive for pearls were entirely unable to go down into the sea.
Then God sent a small fish,
and it entered into its ear and killed it.
And it was washed up by the waves and cast outside.
And since fire could not cook its flesh,
they dried it in the sun, ground it, and ate it.
And at this time, they brought to Abdallah ibn Tahir, the governor of Khorasan, a boy who was born from his mother in that very year,
and had reached the stature of a man,
and his beard had come out,
a matter that is above nature. And in the year
one thousand one hundred and forty-six [of the Greeks],
there was a flood from the river of Zibatrah in the night,
and it destroyed the wall and swept away the houses,
and three thousand people drowned inside the houses.
And in the Tigris also there was a flood,
and it destroyed houses in Baghdad.
And in this year an order was issued,
and at the dawn of the Sunday of the Resurrection, the Hagarenes destroyed the church of Mor George of Qube (or of Koke?) and of Mor Ahudemmeh,
on the pretext that they had been newly built.
And Omar, the governor of Melitene, raided into the territory of the Romans,
and Emperor Theophilos met him.
And the Romans defeated the Arabs at first.
And then the Arabs took courage and the Romans fled,
and the Arabs entered the emperor's camp (fossaton),
